B edges ahead because it marks unproven claims with explicit placeholders and answers the 'why don't you carry brand X' objection. Neither puts unavailable brands in the public copy or gives customers a way to check whether their model is covered. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give the team a solid test for knockoff parts based on fit, durability and whether Spindle can stand behind the part, and both avoid made-up figures. B's rule is easier to act on because it adds a trial-stocking step tracked by returns per part, and its homepage line and alternatives are closer to what the customer cares about, which is getting the appliance fixed.
